requirements.requirement: Repair bin/publish so publishing a release atomically replaces current, with concurrent readers seeing only a complete previous or new release and no missing current path.
requirements.summary: The publisher validates the release, creates a same-directory temporary symlink, and atomically renames it over current. A bounded concurrency test performed 500 publication swaps alongside 3,000 reader checks with zero missing, partial, mixed, unresolvable, or unexpected results.

requirements.requirement: Refuse any release missing MANIFEST without changing the existing current target.
requirements.summary: Publishing the incomplete release returned an error while current's target, inode, and exposed data remained unchanged. The same rejection behavior was verified after restart.

requirements.requirement: Preserve both staged complete releases and keep publication or rollback to either release possible.
requirements.summary: Both release directories and their contents remained intact. Direct tests published release two, rolled back to release one, and republished release two, including after restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy RHEL 9 platform.
requirements.summary: RHEL 9.8 and kernel 5.14.0-687.20.1.el9_8.x86_64 were unchanged before and after execution and restart. The implementation uses available POSIX shell and platform utilities, and package health remained clean.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The mandatory node1 restart protocol is also complete and coherent: it records a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged reboot scheduling, transient connection loss, a different post-restart boot identity corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshot, a running recovered system, preserved release data, unchanged platform, and working rejection and rollback behavior.
limitations: The concurrency guarantee was exercised with a strong but necessarily bounded test of 3,000 reader observations across 500 swaps rather than every possible process schedule.
Requirement preserve_and_rollback cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The publisher replacement was required (cmd-c8f7dd8602144c15); publication and rollback swaps were bounded functional evidence (cmd-a53526ef53784949, cmd-aa81dc90a149479f); the scheduled reboot fulfilled the mandatory restart protocol (cmd-984d30e7081e4bc9); and post-restart rejection/rollback tests restored the intended final target and removed their temporary file (cmd-f50c8156154447b8). Temporary test logs were removed, no failed services or new listening exposure appeared, and package health remained clean.
